call.text: H‑Net builds its hierarchy by applying a dynamic‑chunking layer that uses a routing module to draw content‑dependent chunk boundaries and a downsampler that keeps vectors at those boundary positions, thereby creating a compressed representation that can be further processed in subsequent stages [HNET:1:c012][HNET:T6:r03]. The architecture can be iterated, so that the output of one dynamic‑chunking stage becomes the input to a second, yielding a nested, multi‑stage hierarchy [HNET:3.1:c049]. Empirically, adding the second stage improves performance: H‑Net (2‑stage) is significantly better than H‑Net (1‑stage) [HNET:3.1:c049].
